name: Dual Littlestone Dimension / Effective Range (logarithmic upper bound)
details: For every nonempty finite binary class on a nonempty finite domain, $\mathrm L^*(\mathcal H)\le\lfloor\log_2(\mathrm E(\mathcal H)+2)\rfloor$. Equivalently $\mathrm E\ge2^{\mathrm L^*}-2$, which strengthens the previously recorded affine consequence $\mathrm E\ge\mathrm L^*-1$. Equality holds on the universal class: $\mathrm L^*(\mathcal U_n)=n$ and $\mathrm E(\mathcal U_n)=2^n-2$.
witness_verification: For half-intervals on [n], effective range is n-1, whereas dual Littlestone dimension is floor(log_2 n). Thus effective range cannot be bounded by any affine function of dual Littlestone dimension. The separation follows the upper-bound orientation: parameter 2 grows faster than parameter 1.
